record.body:
## Rationale

Existing deliver efforts have no brief, so an `analyze` check would warn on every old phase until someone backfills them. `init` writes the brief and `settle-phase` reads it. That makes the brief available to agents at the point they plan, and it adds no noise.

## Counter-argument

The marker rule showed that agents follow what a command checks, not what a skill says. A warning from `analyze` for a deliver effort without a brief is the only way to notice a skipped `init` step. The noise is temporary and ends when old efforts are backfilled or a cut-off date excludes them.

payload.alternatives: An analyze warning for a deliver effort without a brief; no settle-phase read
payload.choice: Skills only: init writes the brief and settle-phase reads it; analyze does not check

record.subject: brief-enforcement
